 Meta VR Start Developer Competition: Contest 2026 Official Rules
 THIS CONTEST IS OPEN ONLY TO MEMBERS OF THE META VR START PROGRAM (“ START ”) THAT MEET THE ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA LISTED BELOW.
 NO PURCHASE NECESSARY. A PURCHASE WILL NOT INCREASE YOUR CHANCES OF WINNING.  
 INTERNET ACCESS, META VR DEVELOPER ACCOUNT, AND START MEMBERSHIP ARE REQUIRED TO PARTICIPATE.
 IMPORTANT: PLEASE READ THESE OFFICIAL RULES, WHICH ARE A CONTRACT, CAREFULLY. WITHOUT LIMITATION, THIS CONTRACT INCLUDES INDEMNITIES TO THE SPONSOR FROM YOU AND A LIMITATION OF YOUR RIGHTS AND REMEDIES.  BY PARTICIPATING, YOU AGREE TO BE BOUND BY THESE OFFICIAL RULES AND REPRESENT THAT YOU SATISFY ALL OF THE ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS. VOID WHERE PROHIBITED BY LAW.
 IMPORTANT DATES: 
 EVENT 
 START TIME/DATE 
 END TIME/DATE 
 Entry period: 
 September 24, 2026 at 10:00:00 AM PT
 November 18, 2026 at 12:00:00 PM PT
 Judging period: 
 On or around November  18, 2026
 On or around December 9, 2026
 Winner Announcement: 
                                                       On or around December 11, 2026
 This chart is only a high-level summary of the Contest; read through these entire Official Rules to make sure you understand the details. 
 1. OVERVIEW.  The Meta VR Start Developer Competition: (“ Contest ”) is sponsored by Meta Platforms, Inc., 1 Hacker Way, Menlo Park, CA 94025 (“ Sponsor ”), and encourages developers to develop games and applications for Sponsor’s virtual immersive platform for Meta VR devices. Eligible entrants can enter this Contest as an individual, Team, or Organization (defined below) during the Entry Period.  These Official Rules (“Official Rules”) govern participation in the Contest.  Read through these entire Official Rules carefully to make sure you understand the details.
 2. ELIGIBILITY.   Entry and participation in this Contest is open only to individuals, Teams, and Organizations as defined below (each an “ Entrant ”). As of the start of the Entry Period (as defined above), all Entrants whether as an individual or member of a Team or Organization must: 
 (a) be at least eighteen years of age and the age of majority in their jurisdiction of residence;
 (b) not be residents of, or Organizations domiciled in, Brazil, Quebec, or in any area subject to comprehensive international sanctions such as Crimea, Russia, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, or any other country or individual designated by the United States Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control;
 (c) have an active and valid Meta account with Developer Access enabled or in the case of a Team or Organization be a member of an active and valid Meta account with Developer Access that at least one Team or Organization member has administrative control over; and 
 (d) Representative or person submitting an Entry must be a member of the Meta VR Start Program by the time of submission. 
 Organizations (including corporations, not-for-profit corporations and other nonprofit organizations, limited liability companies, partnerships, and other legal entities) that exist and have been organized or incorporated at the time of entry are eligible to participate in the Contest referred to herein as an “ Organization ”. Organizations that are politically affiliated (as determined by Sponsor in its sole discretion) are not eligible to participate in the Contest.  An association of at least two (2) individuals that does not constitute a legally recognized entity, provided that each natural person comprising such association and meets the eligibility criteria listed above, can submit Entries and are referred to herein as a “ Team ”. 
 Teams and Organizations must appoint and authorize one individual (the “ Representative ”) to represent, act, receive communications, participate, and receive any prize (if awarded), on behalf of the Team or Organization.  By entering on behalf of a Team or Organization, each Representative represents and warrants on behalf of their Team or Organization that they are authorized to act on behalf of their Team or Organization. Sponsor shall have no liability for the acts or omissions of any Representative who acts on behalf of a Team or Organization.
 Entrants may not be under any legal or contractual obligation that would prohibit their participation in the Contest.  Any individual for whom participation in this Contest would mean a violation by them of any applicable law or of any agreement to which they are a party is ineligible to participate. Government and political officials, and employees, officers, directors, members, managers, agents, and representatives of Sponsor, or any other entities participating in the design, promotion, marketing, administration, or fulfillment of this Contest, or any of their respective corporate partners, parent companies, divisions, subsidiaries, affiliates, successors in interest, and advertising, promotion, and public relations agencies and any family (i.e., spouse, partner, parent, legal guardian, child, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, or in-law) or other member of the same household (whether or not related) (“ Released Parties ”) are also not eligible to enter or win this Contest. Any other individual or Organization whose participation in the Contest would create, in the sole discretion of the Sponsor, a real or apparent conflict of interest are not eligible to enter or win this Contest.
 Participation in this Contest constitutes each Entrant’s full and unconditional agreement to and acceptance of these Official Rules and the decisions of Sponsor, which are final and binding in all matters. 
 Entry Limit. Each individual is limited to submitting one (1) Entry in this Contest. For the avoidance of doubt, an Entry is submitted either (i) by an individual on their own behalf, or (ii) by a Team Representative on behalf of a Team or Organization. Participation as a non-Representative Team member does not constitute submitting an Entry.
 Permitted Participation Scenarios. Subject to the one-Entry limit above, an individual may participate in this Contest in any of the following ways:
 (i) as a solo entrant, submitting one Entry on their own behalf;
 (ii) as a solo entrant who submits one Entry on their own behalf and also participates as a non-Representative member of one or more Teams or Organizations (because non-Representative membership does not count as an Entry); or
 (iii) as a Team Representative, submitting one Entry on that Team or Organization’s behalf (and optionally also serving as a non-Representative member of other Teams or Organizations).
 Prohibition. An individual may not both submit an Entry as a solo entrant and serve as a Team Representative, as this would result in two Entries being attributed to that individual. Each individual may serve as the Representative of only one (1) Team or Organization.
 3. HOW TO ENTER. During the Entry Period, eligible Entrants are invited to build and submit an immersive entertainment, gaming, or productivity experience built for Meta VR devices (each a “ Project ”). 
 Entrants may enter by visiting https://start-developer-competition-26.devpost.com/ (“ Contest Website ”) and following the below steps:
 Register for the Contest on the Contest Website by clicking the “Join Hackathon” button. To complete registration, sign up to create a free Devpost account, or log in with an existing Devpost account. 
 Entrants will obtain access to the required developer tools/platform and complete a Project described below in Section 4 (Entry Requirements). Use of the developer tools will be subject to the license agreement related thereto. Entry in the Contest constitutes consent for the Sponsor and Devpost to collect and maintain an Entrant’s personal information for the purpose of operating and publicizing the Contest. 
 Complete and enter all of the required fields on the “Enter a Submission” page of the Contest Website during the Entry Period and follow the requirements below.  
 Successful completion of the steps above, together with all requirements stated in Section 4 (Entry Requirements), including the associated Project, application, videos, and all other Contest-related material or information submitted by an Entrant, constitutes an “ Entry ”.  All Entries, and elements thereof, must comply with the Entry Requirements listed in Section 4 (Entry Requirements) below to be considered for this Contest. 
 Entries must be submitted in full (all steps above must be completed) by Entrant during the Entry Period in strict accordance with the instructions and restrictions in these Official Rules and any other instructions that Sponsor may provide through its authorized representatives or otherwise.  Entries that are not actually completed and received by Sponsor during the Entry Period will not be considered for the Contest.  Purported proof of entry (such as, without limitation, a screenshot of your purported entry) does not constitute proof of actual entry for purposes of this Contest.  Purported entries that are incomplete, received outside the Entry Period, or contain obscene, offensive, or any other language or imagery communicating messages inconsistent with the positive images with which Sponsor wishes to associate itself (all as determined by Sponsor in its sole discretion) or otherwise violate these Official Rules will be void.  Those who do not abide by these Official Rules and the instructions of Sponsor and its representatives and provide all required information may, in Sponsor’s sole discretion, be disqualified, any purported entry by such Entrant void, and Entrant may be excluded from future participation in the Meta VR Start. Any Entry that is infringing, fraudulent, forged, altered, incomplete, lost, late, misdirected, mutilated, illegitimate, incomprehensible, garbled, or generated by a macro, bot, or other automated means will not be accepted and will be void.  Entry made by someone on behalf of any other Entrant or any entity or group, made by another on your behalf (with the exception of a Team or Organization Representative), or originating at any online service other than as specifically described above (including, without limitation, through a commercial promotion subscription, notification, or entering service) will be declared invalid and disqualified for this Contest.  RETAIN A COPY OF YOUR ENTRY AND ALL CONTENT SUBMITTED DURING THE CONTEST, AND ALL RECORDS OF YOUR PARTICIPATION.  SPONSOR IS NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING A COPY OR REPORT OF ANY ELEMENT OF PARTICIPATION.
 4. ENTRY REQUIREMENTS.  Each Entry must meet all of the following requirements, as determined by Sponsor in its sole discretion, or the Entry may be disqualified: 
 Project: Include a Project that meets the following requirements. 
 App Type & Platform: The Project must be a VR/MR application built for  Meta VR devices
 Track: Must align with at least one of the following tracks (each a “Track”). At any time, and at its sole discretion, the Sponsor will have the ability to re-assign a submitted Entry from one Track to another.
 Entertainment: Lean-back media and content experiences—spatial cinema, interactive video, music visualization, immersive storytelling, spatial audio, media companion apps (e.g., commentary tracks, popup production notes, social comments). Content designed to be consumed in any environment. Content designed to be consumed in any environment. Hands-first implementation required.
 Gaming: Games designed for hands-first (required) or eyes and hands. Puzzle, strategy, casual, social, narrative—genres that thrive seated, without controllers.
 Productivity: Apps that make you more effective anywhere or are designed around specific daily moments—multi-panel workspaces, task management, creative tools, or habits tied to a recurring context (morning routine, commute, wind-down). Hands-first implementation required.
 Division: Projects must align with one of the following divisions (each a “Division”). At any time, and at its sole discretion, the Sponsor will have the ability to re-assign a submitted Entry from one Division to another.
 New Experience: Project is conceived of and built within the competition window (starting September 24, 2026). No pre-existing codebases, no shipped titles, no early access builds repurposed
 Adapted / Significantly Updated Experience: Pre-existing project with a meaningful new feature, mode, or platform integration shipped during the competition window. Any build, prototype, or published app that existed prior to September 24, 2026. Sponsor will determine in its own discretion if an update qualifies as significant.
 Examples of Significant Updates: include but are not limited to
 Implementing Hand Interactions as a new feature
 Adding multiplayer support
 Introducing a mixed reality (MR) interaction mode as a new feature
 Releasing a new user generated content creation tool
 Non-Examples: include but are not limited to
 Bug fixes or minor User Interface (UI) tweaks
 Cosmetic changes (e.g., new color scheme)
 Performance optimization without new user-facing features
 Content Experience Requirements & Guidelines: These requirements and guidelines are applicable across all Tracks and Divisions.
 Requirement 
 Standard 
 The Test 
 Hands-first 
 Fully usable with hands end-to-end. Controller support optional. 
 Can someone complete the entire experience without ever pairing a controller? 
 Guidelines 
 Seated-optimized 
 Designed for seated/stationary use. Limit roomscale or large physical movement. 
 The “airplane seat test”—does every interaction work in a 2ft radius? 
 Easy to get into/out of 
 Fast cold start. Clean pause/resume. Satisfying in ≤10 minutes. 
 The “one bus stop test”—can someone have a complete moment in a short ride? 
 Original, not a wrapper 
 Core experience is Entrant-built. Thin wrappers around existing platforms or services (YouTube, ChatGPT, etc.) are highly discouraged. 
 The "take it away test" — remove the third-party service. Is there still a Project? 
 Submission: Project must be submitted during the Entry Period and remain available until the Winner Announcement in one of the following ways:
 For apps built with Unity, Unreal, Godot, Native/Android or another engine: An APK uploaded to the Meta VR Developer Dashboard under a new release channel named “Competition”. 
 For apps built with IWSDK (WebXR) : A link will be required for judges to access and test your application. See " Deploying to GitHub Pages " for additional details. You may also use your preferred hosting solution (e.g., Vercel, Digital Ocean, AWS, Azure, etc).
 All required items must be added to the Submission of the Project on Devpost which includes, but is not limited to:
 Link to your Project in the Competition release channel (from the Meta VR Developer Dashboard) or to your GitHub page (if built with IWSDK / WebXR).
 Demonstration video of your Project that should be less than three (3) minutes and showcase footage of your Project as viewed on a Meta Quest device or via XR Simulator or another equivalent emulator. The video must be uploaded to and made publicly visible on YouTube or Vimeo and a link to the video must be provided on the submission form on the Competition website. Judges are not required to watch beyond three minutes.
 A text description that explains your inspiration, how you built it, future plans for improvement and a target launch date, if not already published to the Meta VR Store. If your Project is an Adapted / Significantly Updated Experience (as described above), Entry should include a summary description of the new features/capabilities added to the application. Screenshots, changelogs and/or demo videos are highly recommended.
 Select the Track you are submitting your Project into: Entertainment, Gaming, or Productivity.
 Select the Division you are submitting your Project into: New Experience or Adapted / Significantly Updated Experience.
 Originality: The Project must be ORIGINAL to each Entrant (or include content that is in the public domain or that is provided to Entrant by Meta specifically for use in the Contest).
 Meta Funding: The Project must not have previously received or currently be receiving direct funding from Sponsor under a separate agreement (e.g., Meta Horizon Start Lifestyle RFP or other development funding from Sponsor).
 Permitted Development Tools: 
 The Project must be built using development tools, SDKs, and resources that are available to the general public and/or to Start Program members. Use of Meta tools, SDKs, or features that have not been released to the Start Program or the general public is not permitted.
 If a Project uses or relies upon any third-party tools, code, or assets, the participant must be authorized to use them in accordance with any terms and conditions or licensing requirements of the tools, code, or assets.
 Policies.  The Project must comply with all relevant Meta / VR Start policies and terms (e.g., Meta VR Start Program Terms , Community Standards , Code of Conduct in VR Policy , Developer App Policies , Developer Content Guidelines , and all other Developer Policies .
 Projects must not include: 
 Any malware, spyware, viruses, or similar harmful code or content or 
 Any content that is false, fraudulent, deceptive, misleading, defamatory, libelous (including trade libel), disparaging, harassing, threatening, profane, obscene, pornographic or otherwise adult-oriented, hateful, indecent, inappropriate, or injurious to any party.
 Projects must be suitable for presentation in a public forum and must follow Meta VR Developer Content Guidelines for 10+, 13+, or 18+ to help keep Meta VR a fun and welcoming place for everyone.
 Language. Projects must be entirely in the English language or include English subtitles. All Entry materials must be in English or, if not in English, the Entrant must provide an English translation of the demonstration video, text description, and testing instructions as well as all other materials submitted. 
 No Violation of 3rd Party Rights or Harms.  
 Projects may not mention or depict any identifiable person other than Entrants.  
 Projects must not infringe, misappropriate, plagiarize, or violate any rights of any third-party including, without limitation, copyright (including moral rights), trademark, trade secret, or rights of privacy or publicity.
 Projects must not contain or describe any harmful or illegal activity or content or in any way violate any federal, state, or local laws, rules, or regulations.
 Projects must not create or imply any association between Sponsor and any individual, entity, or anyone else or his, her, or its products and services.
 Projects must not contain any commercial or corporate advertising (including, without limitation, corporate logos, brand names, and slogans), recognizable branded products, or commercial artwork.
 You agree that your participation in this Contest and agreement to these Official Rules will not violate any agreement to which you are a signatory or party and that no such agreement otherwise limits your ability to participate in this Contest or grant the rights granted by you in these Official Rules. 
 You agree to indemnify the Released Parties against any loss or expense that the Released Parties may sustain or incur on account of any and all claims from any third-party for any use by any Released Party of the Entry authorized pursuant to these Official Rules. 
 Sponsor may at any time disqualify, remove, delete, edit, or restrict access to any Entry, in whole or in part, that violates these Official Rules, the Meta Community Standards, and/or the Conduct in VR Policy.
 Projects must be made available free of charge and with sufficient access until the Winner Announcement to enable viewing, evaluation, use, and testing by Sponsor and Judges (as defined below).  
 Once the Entry Period has ended, you may not make changes or alterations to your submission. The judging process will be based on the state of the Entry at the time of submission deadline. Entries must be capable of successful and consistent operation and function.   
 Entrants must at all times comply with the letter and spirit of 
 the Meta VR Start Program Terms , 
 Supplemental Meta Platforms Technologies Terms of Service  https://www.meta.com/legal/supplemental-terms-of-service/ ) and 
 Meta Terms of Services ( https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms ), 
 and any other use terms, policies, documentation, and other guidelines applicable to any platforms used to develop, host, operate, testing, distribute, and display any Entry or to administer the Contest. This includes the Devpost Terms of Service ( https://info.devpost.com/terms ), which provide additional terms for your participation in the Contest and your use of the Contest website. The Devpost Terms of Service are incorporated by reference into these Official Rules, and the term “Poster” in the Devpost Terms of Service will have the same meaning as “Sponsor” in these Official Rules. If there is a conflict between the Devpost Terms of Service and these Official Rules, these Official Rules shall control with respect to this Contest only.  
 Any attempt to subvert or work-around of such terms and conditions or policies may, in Sponsor’s sole discretion, lead to such Entrant’s disqualification.  
 Sponsor may at any time request written proof of ownership or proper license or use of any material comprising an Entry.  Failure to evidence such proof timely or to Sponsor’s satisfaction may result in ineligibility and disqualification of the Entrant and/or Entry.  
 No technology may be developed, or derived from software that was or is developed, with the direct or indirect aid of financial or preferential support (including but is not limited to development under or with any contract, commercial license or other funding, investment, or support) from Sponsor.  
 Any time prior to the end of the Entry Period, Sponsor may disqualify any Entry or Entrant from receiving a prize in this Contest if Sponsor determines doing so would cause a real or perceived conflict of interest or unfair advantage.
 Sponsor reserves the right in its sole discretion to disqualify any Entrant from the Contest if in Sponsor’s sole discretion the Entrant or Entry does not comply with the Entry Requirements or if Entrant does not comply with any other requirement of these Official Rules.
 5. WINNER SELECTION/NOTIFICATION.  Entries will be evaluated based on the Judging criteria listed below by a panel of experts designated by Sponsor (“Judge(s)”) during the Judging Period. Judges may be employees of the Sponsor or third parties, may or may not be listed individually on the Competition website, and may change before or during the Judging Period. Judging may take place in one or more rounds with one or more panels of Judges, at the discretion of the Sponsor. AI tools may also be used to assist in the judging, but final decisions will be made by human judges.
 Stage One: The first stage will determine via pass/fail whether the Projects meet a baseline level of viability, in that the Project and Entry reasonably fits the theme and reasonably applies the required tools and features featured in the Contest.
 Stage Two: All Entries that pass Stage One will be evaluated in Stage Two based on the below equally weighted criteria (the “Judging Criteria”).
 The scores from the Judges will determine the potential winners of the applicable prizes. The Entrant(s) that are eligible for a Prize, and whose Entries earn the highest overall scores based on the applicable Judging Criteria, will become potential winners of that Prize.
 6. JUDGING CRITERIA  
 Criteria 
 Description 
 Weight 
 Innovation & Creativity 
 Measures originality, creative ambition, and relevance to the chosen track (Gaming, Entertainment, or Productivity). 
 High-scoring projects differentiate themselves, show developer ingenuity, and uniquely leverage Meta device capabilities (e.g., spatial depth, hands-first design) to drive repeat usage.
 25%
 Experience Design 
 Evaluates design, mechanics, and user journey for the intended audience, with emphasis on seated, hands-first, or context-specific use. Strong entries have intuitive navigation, clear onboarding, and a habit-forming purpose.
 Passthrough should be purposeful: the player's real room meaningfully changes the experience, not a scene that plays the same with passthrough off.
 We'll also evaluate FoV-aware design. Since the field of view differs between Meta VR devices, keep essential UI and interactions within a comfortable, narrower FoV and adapt across devices.
 25%
 Technical Implementation 
 Assesses technical expertise, reliability, and strategic use of platform tools, particularly the features that define hands-first experiences: gaze interactions (Unity/Unreal ISDK v207+), hand tracking, passthrough, spatial anchoring, and FoV-aware design.
 High-scoring entries must be performant on Meta Quest hardware (min 60 fps ), solid and bug-free, and show seamless integration of features relevant to their specific track.
 For entries that use passthrough, this includes correct use of scene understanding (MRUK), anchoring content to detected planes, surfaces, and room geometry, and holding up in rooms the developer never tested.
 25%
 Polish & Presentation 
 Assesses the overall quality of the project submission, including UI/UX, art direction, and sound design.  
 High-scoring entries are performant, visually cohesive, and clearly demonstrate relevance to the chosen track. This includes high-quality submission materials (text, images, video) that effectively communicate the project's value.
 On your video/trailer: show real gameplay that honestly represents the experience. Lead with the story and what makes your project distinct. Don't lean on AI-generated video to carry the pitch.
 25%
  In the event of a tie, it will be resolved by Judges’ vote.  Each potential Winner and/or Representative of Winner, all natural people who are members of a winning Team or Organization (as determined and requested in Sponsor’s sole discretion) may be required to complete, execute and return a form presented by Sponsor and other documents (if necessary, which largely affirm the rights granted and obligations contained in these Official Rules) (collectively, the “ Winner Documents ”) according to Sponsor’s instructions. 
 Failure to comply with these requirements, Sponsor’s or its representative’s instructions, or these Official Rules may, in Sponsor’s sole discretion – having due regard of the interests of the potential Winner, result in disqualification from the Contest and forfeiture of any prize potentially won.  
 The Winner Documents, if required, are each subject to verification by Sponsor and may require the Entrant or Representative of Entrant to provide a copy of government-issued identification card or number therefrom. If any prize, prize notification, or other Contest-related communication is returned as undeliverable or if a selected potential Winner or Representative of Winner cannot be reached or does not respond as instructed after Sponsor has attempted to notify that potential Winner, that selected Winner or Representative of Winner may – after Sponsor has taken reasonable efforts to reach the selected Winner or Representative of Winner – be disqualified and an alternate winner may be selected (time permitting and in Sponsor’s sole discretion).  The prize claim and Prize Winner Documents are subject to verification by Sponsor.  The prizes, if legitimately claimed, will be awarded.  Sponsor will not be obligated to pursue more than two (2) alternate winners (time permitting) for any reason.
  7. PRIZES, QUANTITY, AND APPROXIMATE RETAIL VALUE (“ARV”).  
 Limit one (1) prize per Entry determined by Judging Process.

 If a Team or Organization Entrant wins, the prize will be awarded to the Representative.  Sponsor is not responsible for a potential Winner’s inability to accept or use the prize for any reason. Prize details will be decided at Sponsor's sole discretion.  No more than the stated prizes will be awarded.  Sponsor will not replace any lost, mutilated, or stolen prizes or prize elements or any prizes that are undeliverable or do not reach a Winner or Representative because of an incorrect or changed contact information.  If a Winner or Representative does not accept or use the entire prize, the unaccepted or unused part of the prize will be forfeited, and Sponsor will have no further obligation with respect to that prize or portion thereof.  No transfers, prize substitutions, or cash redemptions will be made, except at Sponsor’s sole discretion and as noted above.  Winners or Representatives are strictly prohibited from selling, auctioning, trading, or otherwise transferring any part of the prize, except with Sponsor’s permission, which may be granted or withheld for any reason in Sponsor’s sole discretion. Sponsor reserves the right to substitute any prize or portion thereof with another prize or portion thereof of equal or greater value for any reason, including unavailability of the stated prize.  Each Entrant waives the right to assert as a cost of winning any prize any and all costs of verification and redemption or and any liability and publicity which may arise from claiming or seeking to claim a prize.
 Prizes will be payable to the Entrant, if an individual, or to the Entrant’s Representative, if a Team or Organization. It will be the responsibility of the winning Entrant’s Representative to allocate the prize among their Team or Organization’s participating members, as the Representative deems appropriate without involvement of Sponsor.
